name: Ashwall Geneware Street Preacher's Manifesto Rig
description: A floor-length coat of layered salvage canvas, hand-painted with dense scripture in six languages, split up the back to accommodate a full bioluminescent spine ridge that pulses amber during sermons. Beneath it, a bare-chested wrap of kente-panel cloth across the torso and loose linen trousers with a tail-slot cut at the rear. The coat hem is perpetually singed.
functionality: Back split and tail-slot accommodate full geneware expression; the coat layers provide moderate acid-rain protection.
what_it_says: This person has given their body to their message and wants every passerby to read it.
price_range: Φ15–30 materials cost; labor is devotion
story_hooks: One of the six languages on the coat is a dead corporate cipher — whoever painted it knew something they shouldn't.
The bioluminescent spine ridge flickers irregularly, suggesting an infection or a failing geneware install.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant

physical_description.visual_profile: A dramatic, prophet-like silhouette: floor-length layered coat dominates the frame, creating an almost ecclesiastical presence. The bioluminescent spine ridge visible through the split back reinforces a spiritual, augmented aesthetic. The kente-panel wrap and bare chest suggest ritual exposure and cultural pride. Overall impression: street preacher meets combat mystic.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and flowing through the body; the coat drapes with intentional looseness, allowing movement during animated sermons. The split back is wide enough to fully expose the bio-spine without constraint. Linen trousers sit low and comfortable, with strategic tail-slot tailoring. Not fitted or tactical—deliberately expansive.
physical_description.primary_material: Layered salvage canvas (Ashwall stock—heavy, weathered industrial weave); kente-panel cloth (traditional woven textile, likely reclaimed or artisan-made); loose linen trousers; natural fiber blend throughout
physical_description.texture: Canvas is rough, hand-painted, with visible brush marks and ink saturation. Paint sits atop the weave in places, catching light. Edges are frayed and worn from street use. Kente panels show tight traditional weaving. Linen has a soft, lived-in drape.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant: earthy canvas tan/ochre with dense black and deep indigo scripture lettering. Kente panels introduce vibrant gold, crimson, emerald, and white geometric patterns. Bioluminescent spine: pulsing amber/golden light. Coat hem charred black and grey from repeated flame exposure.
physical_description.closures: No visible fasteners on the coat—appears to be layered and worn open. The wrap likely ties at the torso with natural cord or fabric strips. Trousers cinched with simple rope or elastic.
distinctive_features: Dense hand-painted scripture in six languages covering the entire back and sleeves
Full bioluminescent spine ridge running from shoulders to tailbone, pulsing during sermons
Split back design to accommodate the bio-spine without constraint
Tail-slot cut at rear of trousers (for bio-spine or movement flexibility)
Perpetually singed and blackened coat hem from fire or ritual practice
Kente-panel wrap signals cultural (likely West African diaspora) heritage
Bare chest exposure—deliberately non-armored, spiritually vulnerable
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade salvage with spiritual/cultural dignity. Self-constructed, using found materials, but the kente panels and careful hand-painting suggest intentional artistry rather than mere desperation.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street preacher; religious/spiritual movement; sub-grade ungoverned zone dweller; diaspora cultural pride (West African heritage via kente, multilingual scripture); likely operates in spiritual/community organizing role rather than corporate or military. The bare chest and bioluminescent augmentation suggest willing bodily exposure as part of their ministry—no hiding, no armor.
physical_description.condition_typical: Perpetually weathered and worn. Canvas shows stains, tears, and hand-repairs. Hem is consistently singed (from ritual fire or street conditions). Paint is faded in high-wear areas but dense elsewhere. The bioluminescence compensates for the garment's deterioration, making it luminous and compelling despite physical decay. Looks like it has lived hard, preached hard, survived hard.
